{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My boss constantly invents fake emergencies. Last week he claimed our biggest client was about to leave, so we all worked through the weekend. I later found out the client had just renewed their contract. He does this every month—manufactures crises he knows aren't real because he thinks fear motivates us.

CANDIDATE A:
My boss called an emergency meeting last Tuesday about a major client threatening to leave. We worked late preparing a retention proposal. The client had been unhappy with our service response times, and our quick action saved the account. The warning matched the situation.

CANDIDATE B:
When I was twelve, my dad would burst into my room on school mornings shouting that it was 7 AM and I'd miss the bus. I'd panic and rush. One day I glanced at the kitchen clock on my way out—it was 6:15. He'd been lying about the time for years. He thought fake urgency would make me a more punctual person.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:1"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve authority figures creating false emergencies to manipulate behavior through fear."}
